BreakEvenAnalysis.Context: Year-end review with Harold Kim. Landlord Broadway Astoria Realty hinted at a possible lease bump at renewal, so stress-testing the monthly nut.

CurrentState.Note: MembershipDues line is food sales (covers x avg check); DropIns is bar revenue; EquipmentSales is private events and catering. Labor line covers kitchen and FOH wages; supplies line is food and beverage cost. Reserves feed the $30K emergency operating account.

Scenario_A_RentTo750.Label: Rent increases to $13,000/mo at lease renewal
Scenario_A_RentTo750.BreakEvenCalculation: Monthly nut $96,500 / avg blended check $42 = ~2,298 covers/mo (~85/day, open 27 days; closed Mondays).
Scenario_A_RentTo750.Impact: Manageable. Roughly one extra moderately busy night per week covers it.

Scenario_B_RentTo850.Label: Worst case - rent to $14,000/mo
Scenario_B_RentTo850.Impact: Still profitable but tightens Carlton's draw. Push catering bookings to offset.

BreakEvenAnalysis.KeyInsight: Break-even is roughly 2,300 covers/month (~85/day). We run ~1,450 dine-in covers plus bar and events, so the cushion comes mostly from bar margin and private events. Slow Mondays (closed) already baked in.
ActionItems: Confirm renewal terms with Broadway Astoria Realty before September
Review blended check average with Harold Kim at Q2 close
Keep emergency operating account at $30,000 floor
